---
name: czech-copy
description: Use when writing or editing Czech text on a web page (headings, buttons, paragraphs, meta descriptions). Czech typography rules - quotes, non-breaking spaces after one-letter words, dashes, numbers, abbreviations.
---

# Czech text on the web

- Quotes „like this“ (low 99, high 66), nested ‚like this‘.
- Non-breaking space (` ` in HTML/Astro, U+00A0 in data) after the one-letter
  words **k s v z o u a i** and between a number and its unit (`10 %`, `5 kB`).
- Dash with spaces – like this (en dash); ranges without spaces: 9–17 h.
- Thousands separated by a non-breaking space: 12 500 Kč.
- `s.r.o.` always with periods, likewise `a.s.`.
- Buttons and links: a verb in the imperative or a clear target („Napište nám“,
  „Ceník služeb“), not „Klikněte zde“ ("click here").
- Keep `meta description` between 120 and 160 characters. No period at the end of headings.
- Keep the tone of the surrounding text (formal "vy" address, sentence length). If the
  project has content tests (lengths, card counts), respect them.

name: element-edit
description: Use when a request comes from the webai overlay with a [Selected element] block (selector, text, html, and a source file:line:col when the framework provides one). Explains how to find where the element's content and styles really live and how to make a minimal, safe edit.
---

# Editing an element selected in the overlay

The message starts with a `[Selected element]` block: the CSS selector, the
element's text and an HTML excerpt. With Astro and static HTML it also has
`source: <file>:LINE:COLUMN`, the location of the element's opening tag.

## Finding the element

1. **With `source:`** open that file at that line. `inside:` lists the files
   the component is nested in (parents), which helps when the props passed in
   need to change.
2. **Without `source:`** (React, Vue, Svelte, Next.js, server templates) search
   the sources for the most specific piece first: a distinctive phrase of the
   text, then class names from the selector or the HTML, then the component
   structure around it. Ignore build output. If several places match, pick the
   one whose surrounding markup matches the HTML excerpt.

## Where the content really lives

**The text is often not in the template.** When the element renders an
expression (`{…}` in Astro/JSX/Svelte, `{{ … }}` in Vue and most server
templates), find the source:
- props → where the component is used (`inside:` or grep for the component name),
- the same file's script part (Astro frontmatter `---`, `<script setup>`, top of a JSX module),
- content and data folders (`src/content/**`, Markdown with frontmatter, `src/data/**`,
  `src/config/**`, `src/i18n/**`, JSON/YAML, a CMS export).
Edit the data source, not the template, otherwise the change drifts from the other places.

## Making the change

1. **Component used more than once.** A template change shows up everywhere the
   component is used. Grep for its name. If the user clearly wants the change in
   one place only, add a prop or variant instead of changing it for all, and
   mention it in your answer.
2. **Styles.** First the component's own styles (Astro/Vue/Svelte `<style>`,
   CSS modules next to it), then the project's global CSS or Tailwind classes,
   whatever the project already uses. See the `web-styling` skill.
3. `data-webai-src`, `data-astro-cid-*` and framework-generated class names in
   the HTML are dev server artifacts. Never write them into source files.
4. Do not edit build output or dependencies: `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`,
   `.astro/`, `node_modules/`.

## When the request is unclear

For changes that alter the page structure, ask briefly (one question) instead of guessing.
For small things (text, color, spacing), make the most likely choice and say what you chose.

--- name: stock-images description: Use when the user asks for a photo, illustration or other image that the project doesn't have yet. Covers finding openly licensed images on Openverse, saving them into the project, alt text and the credit line their licenses require. --- # Free images with the right credit - **Search Openverse** (no key needed), only images that may be used on a commercial site and resized or cropped: `https://api.openverse.org/v1/images/?q=&license_type=commercial,modification&mature=false&page_size=8`. Each result has `title`, `creator`, `license`, `license_version`, `width`, `height`, `url` (the file) and `foreign_landing_url` (its page). You can't see the images: pick by title and size, and prefer landscape images at least 1200 px wide for wide spots. - **Save it into the project**, don't hotlink: where the project keeps images (`src/assets/` with `astro:assets`' ``, or `public/images/`). If you have no tool to download a binary file, tell the user the URL and the path to save it to, and write the markup for that path. - **Alt text** says what the image shows in this page's context, not the file name. Purely decorative images get `alt=""`. - **Credit:** licenses other than CC0 and Public Domain Mark (`cc0`, `pdm`) require one. Put it right under the image or in the footer: `Photo: {title} by {creator}, CC {LICENSE} {version}`. Never drop or shorten it when restyling. - Say in your answer which image you chose, from where and under which license.

name: verify-change
description: Use after editing source files from the webai overlay, before answering. How to check the change without starting servers, and how to report what was and was not verified.
---

# Verifying a change

The dev server is running and reloads the change on its own. **Do not run**
`npm run dev`, `astro dev`, `vite`, `next dev` or a build.

1. Re-read the edited section: the template's syntax (closed tags, `{}`
   expressions, Astro frontmatter between `---`, JSX attribute names).
2. If you have shell access and the project has a quick check (`npm run check`,
   `astro check`, `tsc`, lint), run it only for edits that could break types or
   imports. Skip it for text or color changes.
3. The shell is often disabled in the overlay. If you cannot run a check, do not
   work around it. Say in your answer what you did not verify.
4. Answer: one or two sentences on what changed and where (`file:line`), plus
   anything left unverified or affecting other parts of the site.

name: web-styling
description: Use when changing colors, spacing, typography, layout or responsiveness of a web page element. Covers reusing design tokens, keeping WCAG AA contrast, responsive breakpoints and avoiding specificity hacks.
---

# Styling without breaking the site

- **Tokens, not values.** Before writing a color, size or spacing, look for
  custom properties (`grep -n -- '--' src/styles` / `:root`). Use an existing token;
  add a new one only when none fits, and name it by purpose, not by color.
- **WCAG AA contrast:** body text ≥ 4.5 : 1, large text (≥ 24 px, or 18.66 px bold)
  and icons ≥ 3 : 1. When you change a text or background color, compute the contrast and state it in your answer.
- **Responsiveness:** use the breakpoints the project already has (grep `@media`). Do not introduce new
  values. Think the change through for mobile too.
- **Specificity:** no `!important` and no ID selectors to win overrides. Prefer editing
  the original rule. In a scoped Astro `<style>`, styles apply only to that component;
  reaching children of other components needs `:global()`.
- **Motion:** wrap animations in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.
- **Hiding content:** `display: none` on content is often a mistake. Make sure the user really wants
  to hide the element, not just move it.

# @jantcz/webai

[![Socket Badge](https://socket.dev/api/badge/npm/package/@jantcz/webai)](https://socket.dev/npm/package/@jantcz/webai)

Shift+click any element on your site, say what to change, and an AI coding
agent edits the source: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi, your own
command, or a built-in agent with free models. Development only: nothing ends
up in your build.

```bash
npx @jantcz/webai ./site                           # a folder of HTML files
npx @jantcz/webai --target http://localhost:3000   # in front of any running dev server
```

```js
import webai from '@jantcz/webai/vite';            // vite.config: plugins: [webai()]
import webai from '@jantcz/webai/astro';           // astro.config: integrations: [webai()]
import { withWebai } from '@jantcz/webai/next';    // next.config: export default withWebai(config)
import { createWebai } from '@jantcz/webai';       // any Node server: app.use(createWebai().middleware)
```

No install at all: the [WebAI Editor](https://jantcz.github.io/WebAI/editor/)
edits any website in the browser.

Documentation, examples and Docker: https://github.com/JanTcz/WebAI

# Agents and skills for webai

A single source for all CLIs. Skills use the Agent Skills standard
(`skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter); subagents
are Markdown files with frontmatter (`agents/<name>.md`).

| CLI | How it picks them up |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `--plugin-dir` pointing at this folder, names `webai:<skill>` |
| Codex | symlinks in `<project>/.agents/skills/`, subagents generated into `.codex/agents/*.toml` |
| Gemini CLI | symlinks in `<project>/.agents/skills/` and `<project>/.gemini/agents/` |

The overlay creates the symlinks the first time a given agent is used and never
overwrites an existing file of the same name.

Subagents have no `tools` field: tool names differ between CLIs, so the
read-only restriction lives in the instruction text.

---
name: a11y-reviewer
description: Read-only accessibility review of recently changed Astro/HTML/CSS files - heading order, alt texts, link and button names, color contrast, focus visibility. Use after a visual or structural change when the user asks for a check, or for larger edits.
---

You are an accessibility reviewer. **Do not edit anything**; only read files and report findings.

In the changed files, check:
- heading order (no skipped levels, one `h1` per page),
- `alt` on images (decorative ones `alt=""`), names for buttons and links without text (`aria-label`),
- text contrast against the background based on CSS variables (AA: 4.5 : 1, large text 3 : 1),
- visible focus (`:focus-visible`) and that interactive elements are `a`/`button`, not `div`,
- `lang` and meaningful link text.

Output: a list of findings `file:line – problem – suggested fix`, sorted by
severity. If everything is fine, say so in one sentence.

---
name: copy-editor
description: Read-only copy review of text changed on the website - typography (quotes, non-breaking spaces, dashes), grammar, tone consistency, CTA wording. Follows the czech-copy skill for Czech sites. Use when the user asks to proofread or after larger text edits.
---

You are a proofreader of website copy. **Do not edit anything**; only read and suggest.

Work in the language of the site (check `lang` and the surrounding text). For
Czech, follow the rules of the `czech-copy` skill (quotes „“, non-breaking
spaces after k s v z o u a i, dashes, numbers, `s.r.o.`); for other languages,
apply that language's standard typography. Also watch grammar, agreement,
consistent form of address and the length of `meta description`.

Output: a list of `file:line – original → suggested – why`. If there are no findings, one sentence.
